boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Petersburg record (April 2, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. Sutherland's Station (VA090) is the same day and is a separate record; the March 25 picket-line captures belong to Fort Stedman (VA084). Humphreys commanded the Second Corps, and his account of its actions here is a participant's. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Armies' and the live field zero. Humphreys says the works in front of Ord and Wright were held by four brigades of Hill's corps under Wilcox, about 4,000 enlisted men by the February 20 return, and those in front of Parke by Gordon's corps, about 7,600 by the same return, and relays Wilcox that Fort Gregg held 200 infantry; Lee wrote that the brigades on Hatcher's Run were cut off.
claims.rationale: February return strengths assigned to formations, not April 2 counts; the Union assaulting force is described by corps only. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Humphreys, following Wright, says the point of assault was chosen after personal examination and the reports of officers who had long scanned the works, and that the attack could not have succeeded without the picket line taken on March 25; Lee reported on April 2 that the enemy had broken through and intercepted his brigades. Humphreys says Ord's secret march with part of the Twenty-fourth Corps left the enemy in ignorance of it until April 2, but Lee's April 1 letter reports prisoners taken that day from the Twenty-fourth Corps and a belief that most of it was south of the James.
claims.rationale: Attributed knowledge from an interested history and dispatches. Humphreys' 'ignorance' and Lee's April 1 report conflict and are not reconciled; Lee's letter records a belief, not a complete order of battle.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Humphreys says the Sixth Corps gained the whole front of attack, Parke took the works on either side of the Jerusalem plank road but not a rear line, Fort Gregg was taken, and Lee's intrenchments were found abandoned at three in the morning of April 3; Lee wrote that he must abandon his position that night.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The fall of Petersburg and Richmond is a campaign consequence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 7,750 (US 3,500; CS 4,250) and the live field 8,746 (US 3,894; CS 4,852). Humphreys gives Wright's 1,100 killed and wounded in fifteen minutes, Parke's capture of 12 guns and 800 prisoners, and Gibbon's loss of 714 with two guns and about 300 prisoners taken and 55 dead found in Fort Gregg; he gives no Confederate total.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Corps figures cover different parts of the day's front and are not summed.

open_questions: Grant's report (No. 1, Richmond campaign, pp.50-58), Meade's, Wright's, Parke's, Ord's and Gibbon's reports (Nos. 4, 105, 153, 213; Gibbon's selected and cited under VA092), Wilcox's and Gordon's accounts, the Union casualty return (No. 2) and the Confederate returns remain deferred. Lee's April 1 letter (selected) also reports Dinwiddie and Five Forks; only its prisoners passage is cited here.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
